memo.recommendation: Prioritize playback, because its top specific issue, `playback.general`, is ranked first in the business ranking and has priority score {C6}. This follows the issue-level decision rule, even though usability has the largest area-level severity sum {X5}.
memo.supporting_evidence: `playback.general` covers music stopping or restarting, playback failures, and false offline reports; its mean severity is {C5}, a secondary consideration. A customer reports that music keeps stopping [review:98333d3d-0049-4711-a8c9-8daf98e04479]. In the baseline, `other.general` ranks first with priority score {C3}, but it is a broad catch-all and is excluded from the business ranking; it has complaint count {C1} and mean severity {C2}. The next business-ranked specific issue is `billing.paywall_named_feature`, with priority score {C9}; a customer describes losing access to repeat controls [review:98fee45a-083f-4315-a7f5-3a66f9bd22fd].
memo.alternatives: Usability was not selected despite having the largest area-level severity sum {X5}; its leading listed issue, `usability.ads`, ranks behind `playback.general` in the business ranking and has priority score {C12}. Billing/support ranks below playback by area severity sum {X11}, and its leading listed issue, `billing.paywall_named_feature`, also ranks behind `playback.general` with priority score {C9}. Access has the smallest area-level severity sum among the four areas {X2}; its first listed issue, `access.login`, ranks below the issues cited above in the business ranking. The recommendation therefore follows the specified issue-level rule rather than selecting the largest area total.
memo.sensitivity: If named-feature paywall complaints were severity two instead of three, the top issue would remain `other.general`; the sensitivity check gives it priority score {X24}, compared with {X25} for `playback.general} and {X26} for `billing.paywall_named_feature`. Thus the sensitivity result does not change the top specific issue after excluding the catch-all, and playback remains the recommendation under the issue-level rule.
memo.limitations: The evidence consists of self-selected, public, historical Google Play reviews from an eighteen-month window ending in November, not a representative sample of Spotify users. There is no revenue, plan-tier, or confirmed churn data; stated cancellation intent is not observed churn. Model labels have imperfect agreement with human labels and an independent verifier, and fixed feature-word rules may leave distinct problems hidden within broad groups. Rankings exclude quarantined reviews {X21} and any unclassified reviews; the reported pending unclassified count is {X22}.
